page_title: Wayfinder — Turn AI collaboration into a reviewable voyage map

sources.entry: Wayfinder - Local-first visual voyage map for preserving Codex and Claude Code sessions, branches, failures, decisions, and file changes. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/StayCurious-Xuan/wayfinder) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Wayfinder
summary.one_liner: A local-first desktop app that organizes AI coding sessions (currently Codex and Claude Code) into a reviewable project "voyage map" of goals, branches, failures, decisions, and file changes.
keywords: record how ai solved a problem
use_cases: Reviewing how an AI coding task was reached, including dead ends
Tracing a conclusion back to the session or file change that produced it
Comparing different AI tools' attempts under one goal
Reusing validated problem-solving methods from past work
Keeping a record of tests, rollbacks, and rejections in AI-assisted projects
summary.what_it_does: Wayfinder runs as a desktop app that reads new local session records from Codex and Claude Code in the background. It groups goals, replies, tool actions, and file changes into the matching project automatically, without requiring changes to how the user works with those tools. The result is a visual map of each project's voyages and branches, where the user can compare attempts and jump back to the original session and file evidence. It keeps failed routes, tests, rollbacks, and rejections traceable, and when sources disagree it keeps each side's evidence rather than producing a verdict. All data is described as kept locally.
notable: Builds the map automatically from local Codex and Claude Code session records
Merges attempts from different AI tools under one goal into a single voyage
Links conclusions back to the matching session, file change, or validation result
Listed as open source on GitHub (StayCurious-Xuan/wayfinder) in awesome-mac, tagged as freeware
caveats: The current public build only supports Codex and Claude Code as sources
Only captures evidence that was actually recorded; it does not invent missing evidence
